rounds.plan: Survey all four directions before moving.
Check the unsurveyed direction and advance if open.
Survey the new cell for an open route or beacon.
Avoid the close reflection and probe the apparently open side passage.
The way ahead is mirrored; inspect the left passage.
Test the apparently open corridor ahead.
A mirror blocks the way ahead; survey the other three directions.
Take the untried corridor with purple floor markers.
Survey this mirrored junction for a real opening or green beacon.
Probe the only unsurveyed direction from this junction.
Survey this mirrored junction for a real passage or green beacon.
Backtrack along the known route to an earlier junction with an untried branch.
The route ahead is a mirror; probe the left-side passage.
Return to the previous junction and resurvey its branches.
Follow the open branch away from the mirrored dead end.
Ahead is a mirrored wall; survey the other directions for an opening.
Return through the known corridor and inspect the unexplored north branch.
Backtrack to the main junction and face its untried east branch.
Return to the far end of the explored corridor and probe beyond it.
Advance toward the distant reflection; the next cell appears open.
Ahead is a mirror; survey the other directions for a real opening or beacon.
Probe the open-looking corridor ahead from this mirrored junction.
Survey this mirrored cell for a real opening or green beacon.
Backtrack from the mirrored dead end and probe the side passage.
Return to the adjoining junction and recheck its north branch.
Ahead is a mirror; inspect the two remaining unexplored directions.
North and south are mirrors; take the open east passage.
The forward route is mirrored; inspect the remaining directions for an opening.
Backtrack from the dead-end branch to the starting junction and resurvey it.
Go north to the first unsurveyed junction and inspect both side branches.
Return to the far end of the known corridor and recheck its apparent walls.
Probe the eastern corridor, then survey for a real branch or beacon.
Probe the open east passage, then survey the new cell for the beacon.
Take the open north passage and survey the new cell for a branch or beacon.
Continue east along the open corridor and survey the new cell.
North and east are close mirrors; probe the open west passage and survey the new cell.
Probe the remaining corridor and survey the next cell for a real opening or beacon.
Continue north along the apparently open corridor toward the next cell.
A green beacon is visible to the right; turn to inspect whether that route is real.
The beacon is visible only through a mirror; check the remaining side passage.
Return to the unexplored forward corridor and probe the next cell.
Backtrack from the mirrored dead end and inspect the side passage at the previous junction.
A green beacon is visible off to the right; inspect that direction for a real route.
Probe the north side passage near the green reflection, then survey if it opens.
Probe the remaining straight corridor beyond the next cell, then survey for a real branch.
Side walls are mirrors; continue along the open forward corridor.
Survey this mirrored junction for a real opening or green beacon.
Follow the open north corridor and survey the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
Side walls are mirrors; take the open reverse corridor and survey the next cell.
Backtrack to the start and probe its unexplored south passage.
Follow the known east corridor and probe its remaining south exit.
At the northwest boundary, turn to inspect the only unexplored southward route.
North and south are mirrors; inspect the remaining eastward passage.
Advance one cell along the open corridor, then inspect the new view.
Advance along the open corridor, then survey the new cell for a real branch or beacon.
Advance into the open cell ahead, then inspect the closer junction for a real branch.
Return to the far-west cell and probe its unexplored southward branch.
Backtrack to the top corridor and probe the unexplored south branch.
The south branch is a mirror; inspect the remaining eastward route.
Advance along the open corridor and survey the new cell for a real branch or beacon.
Probe the southward passage, which appears open beyond the nearby reflections.
The forward view is a close reflection; survey for a real opening or beacon.
Return to the top corridor and probe its untried south branch.
Continue east along the top corridor and survey the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
Continue east along the open corridor, then survey the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
Continue along the open corridor and inspect the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
Avoid the close side mirrors and continue along the open corridor.
Survey this cell to distinguish real passages from the reflected green beacons.
Take the more open westward corridor; the close robot views are mirror reflections.
The forward view is a reflection; survey the other directions for a real passage or beacon.
This is a mirrored dead end; backtrack through the only open passage.
Continue along the remaining open corridor from this junction.
Ahead appears mirrored; survey the other directions for a real opening or beacon.
Backtrack from this mirrored dead end and resurvey the previous junction.
Two sides are mirrors; take the remaining open corridor away from the arrival route.
The forward view is a reflection; survey the other directions for a real passage or beacon.
Backtrack from the mirrored dead end and resume systematic exploration.
Continue along the open corridor, then survey for an untried branch or beacon.
The current view is a close mirror; turn toward the open corridor and advance one cell.
Survey this mirrored junction for a real passage or nearby green beacon.
The side views are close mirror reflections; inspect the remaining forward route.
Probe the remaining corridor; use the result to distinguish open floor from reflection.
Survey the other directions to distinguish a real passage from the reflections.
Backtrack two cells from the mirrored dead end, then resurvey the earlier junction.
Probe the remaining open-looking side passage near the reflected beacons.
Backtrack one cell and inspect the untried south branch.
The south branch is mirrored; survey the other directions for a real route toward the beacon.
Take the open corridor; the close frontal robot view indicates a mirror.
The front is a confirmed mirror; probe the left-hand passage.
Ahead is a close mirror; inspect the right-hand route toward the green columns.
Probe the open-looking corridor toward the visible green columns.
Advance along the open corridor; the green columns appear only in side reflections.
Survey the mirrored junction for a real opening and direct beacon view.
Backtrack along the only open passage and survey the previous junction for an untried branch.
The front is a mirror; turn around and take the untried open passage.
Return to the far-west branch and probe its untried south and east exits.
The front is a mirror; survey the other directions for an open route or real beacon.
Probe the side passage with one open cell, then survey for a real branch or beacon.
Probe the open-looking side passage; the small centered robot is a distant reflection.
A close frontal robot confirms a mirror ahead; survey the other three directions.
Probe the only untried southward passage from this cell.
The way ahead is a mirror; survey the other directions for an open passage or beacon.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the remaining side passage.
Survey the new cell for a real passage or direct green beacon.
Advance along the apparently open corridor to inspect the next cell.
A close frontal robot confirms a mirror ahead; survey the other directions for a real passage or beacon.
Probe the open-looking side corridor; the distant robot indicates a farther reflection.
The forward view is a close mirror; survey the other directions for a real passage or beacon.
The right side is a close mirror; probe the opposite side passage before backtracking.
Ahead is a close mirror; survey the other directions for a real passage or green beacon.
Both side views are close mirrors; backtrack through the open passage and inspect the next junction.
The last move confirmed a mirror, not the exit; continue along the perpendicular open corridor and survey.
Probe the untried side corridor; the close frontal robot views are mirrors.
Ahead is a close mirror; survey the other directions for a real exit or beacon.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the corridor with the distant reflection.
The forward route is now a close mirror; survey the remaining directions for a real opening or beacon.
Follow the corridor with the distant reflection; the closer views are mirrored walls.
Survey this junction for a direct green beacon and identify the least reflective exit.
Take the corridor with the distant reflection, then survey the next cell for a real exit or beacon.
The confirmed mirror is behind; probe this corridor with the more distant reflection.
Ahead is a close mirror; survey the other directions for an open passage or direct green beacon.
Probe the open corridor with the distant reflection, then reassess for a real beacon.
A close frontal reflection blocks the way; survey the other directions for a real opening or beacon.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the opposite corridor with the distant reflection.
The forward cell is a mirrored wall; survey the other directions for a genuine opening or beacon.
Backtrack through the known corridor to a junction with untried exits.
Advance toward the distant reflection, then survey for a real branch or green beacon.
Take the corridor with the distant reflection; the other three views are close mirrors.
The forward reflection is getting closer; survey for a real branch or green beacon.
Head east through known cells and probe the unvisited eastern branch.
Backtrack to the southwest frontier and inspect its untried south passage.
Ahead is a close mirror; turn left to inspect a possible side exit.
The current view is a close mirror; inspect the two remaining directions for a real exit.
Check the untried east passage at the next junction for a shortcut into the central maze.
East and north are mirrors; probe the remaining south passage before backtracking west.
The way ahead is a close mirror; survey the remaining directions for a real exit or beacon.
Take the open west branch, then survey the new cell for a real exit or beacon.
North and west are close mirrors; probe the remaining south passage and survey the next cell.
North is open, east is a close mirror, and west is the arrival route; continue north to the next junction.
Forward is a confirmed mirror; survey the other three directions for a real opening or beacon.
The confirmed walls leave south as the only untried passage; take it and survey the next cell.
Return to the eastern branch and survey its untried exits.
North and east are close mirrors; take the untried west passage and survey the next cell.
This cell has three mirrored walls; backtrack through its only open exit and resurvey the junction.
Advance along the open corridor, then survey for a real branch or green beacon.
Advance along the open corridor toward the distant reflection, then reassess for a real branch or beacon.
Survey this mirrored cell for a direct green beacon and a real exit.
This is a mirrored dead end; backtrack through the open corridor and reassess at the next cell.
The forward wall is confirmed by the close reflection; survey all remaining directions for a real exit or beacon.
Take the side corridor with the farther reflection and advance toward its junction.
The forward wall is confirmed; survey this cell for a genuine side exit or direct beacon.
Two directions are confirmed mirrors; probe the remaining side corridor and survey the next cell for a real beacon.
Backtrack from the mirrored dead end and inspect the previous junction's north passage.
Advance along the open north passage, then survey for a direct beacon or real branch.
East looks open while north and west are close mirrors; probe east and reassess.
Advance one cell along the open corridor, then survey for a direct beacon or genuine branch.
Follow the untried side corridor for two cells, then survey for a real branch or beacon.
Probe the only untried side corridor, then survey the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
North and east are close mirrors; take the open west branch and survey the next cell for a real beacon.
Take the untried side corridor, then survey the next cell for a real branch or beacon.
Follow the long open corridor to its far end, then survey for a real branch or beacon.
Three close reflections mark mirrors; retreat through the open corridor behind.
This dead end is enclosed by mirrors; backtrack two cells and resurvey the previous junction.
This cell has two mirrored walls; take the untried west passage away from the known dead-end corridor.
Ahead is a close mirror; survey the other directions for a real passage or direct beacon.
Return to the far end of the southern corridor and inspect its untried exits.
Backtrack from the dead end and probe the junction's untried side passage.
Backtrack from the mirrored dead end and survey the previous junction for an untried branch.
Probe the corridor with the distant reflection, then survey for a real branch or green beacon.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the untried side corridor with the distant reflection.
Ahead is a close mirror; survey the remaining directions for a real opening or green beacon.
Probe the corridor ahead to distinguish the reflection from a real opening.
Backtrack from the confirmed mirror and resurvey the previous junction for an untried branch.
Advance along the open corridor toward the next junction, then reassess for a real beacon.
Survey all remaining directions for a direct green beacon or unobstructed passage.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the side corridor with the distant reflection, then survey for a real branch or beacon.
Front and left are close mirrors; probe the untried rear corridor and survey the next cell.
Take the untried open side corridor, then survey for a direct beacon or genuine branch.
Follow the corridor without a close robot reflection, then survey for the actual green beacon.
Avoid the close mirror and probe the side corridor with the farther reflection.
Turn toward the visible green beacon on the left to inspect a possible route.
The beacon is behind a mirror; return to the prior corridor and probe forward.
Inspect the right-hand passage toward the visible green beacon.
The green beacon is only a sliver beside a reflection; survey the other directions for a direct approach.
Advance through the open corridor and survey for a direct route to the nearby beacon.
Two sides are close mirrors; continue along the open corridor and survey the next cell for a direct beacon route.
Advance along the only open corridor and survey for a direct route to the nearby green beacon.
Backtrack through the only open passage, then survey for a direct approach to the nearby green beacon.
Take the untried west branch and survey the new cell for the beacon.
Continue along the open corridor, then survey for a direct route to the green beacon.
Advance along the open corridor, then inspect the leftward route toward the green beacon.
The left view is a mirror; continue up the open corridor and inspect the beacon side.
Return to the open corridor, advance one cell, and survey for a direct beacon approach.
Advance through the open corridor and survey for a direct route to the actual green beacon.
Follow the open corridor toward the distant reflection, then survey for a direct beacon approach.
Enter the open corridor and inspect the nearby green beacon from its side.
Survey the mirrored junction, then continue along the known open corridor.
Turn toward the nearby green beacon markers on the right.
Approach the reflected beacon row, then sweep both lateral directions for the actual green cell.
Pursue the nearby beacons, then make a broad final corridor sweep.
